 Lauri Markkanen (wrist) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 Markkanen sprained his right wrist during Monday’s loss to the Grizzlies and did not play on Wednesday against the Spurs. If he can play on Saturday, Josh Green will likely head to the bench.

 Lauri Markkanen (wrist) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 Markkanen, who missed a game earlier this season with a sprained right wrist, is back on the injury report for the same reason. Josh Green replaced him in the starting lineup in an October 28 game against the Spurs and could do the same on Sunday if Markkanen can’t play. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen scores 24 points (8-of-20 FGs), eight rebounds, an assist, and eight 3-pointers in 112-100 loss to Mavericks on Friday. 
 Lauri was wincing and grabbing his wrist late in the fourth after getting in a tangle for a rebound, so that will be something to monitor to see if he shows up on the injury report. He scored primarily on 3’s in this game which helped the Jazz stay in this game for as long as they did. After a slow start with the injury, Lauri has really started to come along and provide you with the value that you were expecting where you drafted him in the middle rounds of redraft leagues. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen had 21 points (6-of-15 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), ten rebounds, four assists, a steal, two blocks, and five 3-pointers in 120-113 loss to the Pelicans. 
 Lauri Markkanen had a slower start but really got going in the fourth quarter. Lauri hasn’t had the season that many hoped he would but tonight was a good bounce back performance. The Jazz ran some actions to get him open in the fourth quarter so he was able to get some good open looks. He hit a big three in the final minute that helped the Jazz take the lead. He’s just not someone who will create his own shot but is one of the better role players in the NBA.
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen had 22 points (8-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers against the Spurs on Monday. 
 Markkanen’s 22 points were a game-high, though the Jazz still lost by 22 to the Spurs. He bounced back nicely after scoring just 13 points on 14 attempts in Saturday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. Markkanen and the Jazz have three more games this week with their next matchup against the Pelicans on the road Wednesday. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Lauri Markkanen accounted for 13 points (3-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals, two blocks and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Back on the court after missing Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with a right wrist injury, Markkanen played 29 minutes on Saturday before fouling out. Given the injury he was returning from, it wasn’t too surprising to see Markkanen shoot 2-of-11 from beyond the arc. Utah plays four games next week, starting with the Spurs on Monday. Hopefully, Markkanen is sharper than he was against Portland.

 Lauri Markkanen (wrist) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Markkanen is dealing with a sprained right wrist that he suffered Monday against the Grizzlies. Without Markkanen, Kyle Filipowski figures to see enough minutes to make him a worthwhile streamer. 
 Lauri Markkanen 
 UTA 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 According to the Utah Jazz X.com account, Lauri Markkanen suffered a right wrist sprain in Monday’s matchup with the Grizzlies and is considered day-to-day. 
 With Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) out for 6-8 weeks, Utah’s frontcourt rotation is suddenly very thin. Markkanen’s absence should mean more run for Kyle Filipowski, making him a worthwhile waiver wire add. 
 Mo Bamba 
 UTA 
 Center 
 #44 
 Mo Bamba started the second half and finished with 14 points (7-of-8 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist and four blocks on Monday against the Grizzlies. 
 Both Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) and Lauri Markkanen (wrist) exited early from this game, which allowed Bamba and Josh Green to start the second half. Green wasn’t productive, but Bamba made the most of the opportunity. If Jackson remains out against the Spurs on Wednesday, Bamba may be in line to start. However, it is unlikely he produces to this level again, and the matchup against Victor Wembanyama isn’t ideal.

 Nikola Jokić finished Saturday’s win over the Pacers with 19 points (7-of-20 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 13 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer.
 Jokić didn’t shoot well on Saturday, making six of his 17 two-point attempts. The good news for fantasy managers was that the three-time MVP committed just one turnover while finishing two assists shy of a triple-double. Jokić didn’t shoot efficiently, but his ball security kept fantasy managers from taking a major hit in two categories. The Nuggets play three games next week, starting with the Rockets on Monday.
